importantNotes: The return from exile fulfilled Jeremiah's prophecy of 70 years of captivity.
Cyrus the Persian king issued the decree allowing Jews to return — fulfilling Isaiah 44:28.
Ezra 7:10 shows the model for spiritual leadership: study, practice, then teach.
The rebuilt Temple was less glorious than Solomon's, causing older Jews to weep (3:12).
Ezra's prayer of confession (ch. 9) is a model of corporate repentance.

chapters.1: King Cyrus of Persia decrees that the Jews may return to Jerusalem to rebuild the Temple.
chapters.2: The list of exiles who returned to Jerusalem and Judah.
chapters.3: The altar is rebuilt and sacrifices resume; the foundation of the new Temple is laid.
chapters.4: Opposition arises; enemies halt the Temple construction through political schemes.
chapters.5: Prophets Haggai and Zechariah encourage rebuilding; work resumes.
chapters.6: King Darius confirms Cyrus's decree; the Temple is completed and dedicated with joy.
chapters.7: Ezra the scribe arrives in Jerusalem with a royal commission from King Artaxerxes.
chapters.8: The list of those who returned with Ezra; the journey and safe arrival.
chapters.9: Ezra discovers the people have intermarried with pagan nations; his prayer of confession.
chapters.10: The people confess their sin and agree to separate from foreign wives.
